forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. The 45-day extension (announced May 15) held through EOD May 22. Neither the US State Department nor the Lebanese Foreign Ministry issued any statement declaring the ceasefire void. The ceasefire remained porous — IDF struck 30+ targets in south Lebanon (Harouf, Borj El Chmali, Debaal), Hezbollah claimed responsibility for ~10 retaliatory attacks — but neither party withdrew formal sponsorship. Pentagon military coordination track scheduled May 29 remained intact. Next talks set Washington June 2-3. Resolution criteria not met: no formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support; pre-truce intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) not observed. Source: PBS NewsHour, CFR ceasefire tracker, UNRWA Situation Report #10, Times of Israel liveblog May 23.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.name: IDF airstrike on Beirut governorate within 72h of ceasefire extension
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; mass rocket fire historically triggers Israeli large-scale response and truce void.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.55. Three converging developments from May 22-24 justify a major upward move. First: Trump on May 23 posted on Truth Social that 'An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization' (CNN, NPR, PBS confirmed independently). Second: Axios on May 24 reported a 60-day MOU draft had been agreed to by top negotiators — including VP Vance, Witkoff, Kushner, and Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf — with specific terms: Hormuz opens without tolls, Iran never pursues nuclear weapons, US lifts port blockade and issues sanctions waivers. Third: Washington Times exclusive reported US and Iran expected to announce draft by Sunday afternoon. Iranian IRNA quoted a spokesperson: 'the trend has been toward narrowing differences.' However, two material countervailing facts prevent a higher probability: Trump himself told Axios it is '50/50' whether a 'good deal' or 'blow them to kingdom come'; and Iranian state media (Times of Israel May 23 liveblog) reported Iranian media saying Strait of Hormuz will stay under Iran's management — contradicting the Axios MOU draft terms. No signed document has been publicly confirmed by both Reuters and an official Iranian Foreign Ministry or US State Dept press release. The resolution criteria requires principal confirmation, not draft-stage reporting. Probability therefore sits at 0.55 — above baseline given concrete draft progress, below 0.65 given the principal-level mixed signals and 50/50 Trump framing.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. MOU draft reported by US outlets but not confirmed by Iranian principal-level source = NOT resolved.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; direct principal-level engagement removed the Pakistani-channel lag in April.

indicators.name: Trump public statement calling deal 'beautiful' or 'done'
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; Trump's May 23 'largely negotiated' post is a partial trigger; 'done' or formal announcement would fully trigger.

forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.48. The MOU draft (Axios May 24) explicitly provides that during the 60-day period the Strait of Hormuz would open with no tolls and Iran would agree to clear mines. If the MOU is signed by Sunday May 24 (as multiple sources reported as the target), a 50-vessel/day window before June 10 — 17 days away — becomes physically achievable. Current transit rate: AIS data showed only 2 confirmed vessels on May 23 and IRGC-announced figure of 25/day (unverifiable; excludes dark-fleet). MSC launched a Hormuz-bypass service May 10 and has not announced a return. Maersk transited one vessel under US escort May 4 (Project Freedom) but no scheduled resumed service. Lloyd's war-risk premium remains elevated — LMA survey as of May 6 showed premiums still up to 8x pre-war baseline, and LMA stated 'safety concerns, not insurance availability, are driving reduced traffic.' The 17-day window to June 10 is tight for physical mine-clearing, insurer re-rating, and shipping line scheduling. Probability moved upward from deal proximity but constrained by operational lead time even in an optimistic scenario.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22 → 0.27. The Knesset dissolution bill passed a preliminary reading 110-0 on May 20 (Al Jazeera, Jerusalem Post, Haaretz confirmed). Netanyahu was absent from the vote, a documented posture of non-endorsement. The bill still requires three additional readings before becoming law; the House Committee must then set an election date at least 90 days out. At no point between May 19-24 has Netanyahu made a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date. The resolution criteria require either a formal Netanyahu announcement or a passed dissolution motion — neither has occurred. Netanyahu's counter-strategy is to revive the Haredi draft exemption bill as a side-deal to buy coalition time (Times of Israel, May 24). Probability moves modestly upward due to the dissolution bill's institutional momentum, but the 8-day remaining window to June 1 for a formal announcement remains low-probability given Netanyahu's documented preference for late-October elections.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts. The preliminary reading of the dissolution bill (May 20) does NOT count as a passed dissolution motion — three more readings required.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.35 → 0.52 at Sunday cold-start review. Two material developments since last reasoning (May 19) warrant a significant upward revision. First: the coalition's own bill to dissolve the Knesset passed a preliminary reading 110-0 on May 20 (all MKs present voted in favour, including coalition members). This is an institutional action, not merely a threat — the dissolution mechanism is now in motion. Second: polling data published May 19-20 (Times of Israel) shows the pro-Netanyahu bloc at only 49-51 seats in current polling, 10 seats short of a majority. The current formal coalition retains approximately 49 seats per Jerusalem Post Facebook report, already below the 61-seat threshold in de-facto terms due to Degel HaTorah's declared 'no trust' stance (May 12). The coalition's own submission of a dissolution bill — while Netanyahu was absent — is a structural signal that the coalition no longer believes it can hold together through October. However, uncertainty remains: dissolution still requires three more readings; Netanyahu is actively reviving the Haredi draft exemption bill as a retention mechanism; Smotrich has not formally departed; and the Codex ambiguity rule specifies that polling alone does not resolve. Cold-start base rate from first principles: Israeli governing coalitions with a < 55-seat effective bloc and an internal dissolution bill in progress have collapsed in 80%+ of historical cases; however the 5-month remaining window and Netanyahu's institutional resource advantage temper this to ~50-55%. Judge selects 0.52.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. If dissolution bill passes all three readings: counts as YES at that point regardless of subsequent coalition maneuvering. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES if observed; would also trigger Haredi reconsideration.

indicators.name: Degel HaTorah files formal dissolution motion in Knesset
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; coalition's own dissolution bill already advanced to preliminary reading May 20 — formal Degel HaTorah-sponsored motion is the next confirmatory step.

forecasts.question: Will the US-Iran active military ceasefire (currently informal, held since approximately March 2026) be extended or formalized via a signed document lasting at least 30 days beyond EOD 2026-06-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. MOU draft reported by Axios May 24 includes a 60-day ceasefire extension framework with Hormuz reopening and nuclear negotiation commitments. Trump's 'largely negotiated' statement and Washington Times exclusive reporting expected announcement by Sunday May 24 afternoon. Even if this specific announcement slips, the structural ceasefire has held for ~86 days. Base rate for ceasefire extension given ongoing active talks, Pakistan mediation, and both sides' economic pressure is high. However Trump's '50/50' framing, IRGC hardline media pushback, and no signed document yet introduce material downside. Separate from F3 (which requires a written framework on the nuclear/Hormuz question) — this forecast asks only whether the bilateral military pause extends through June 15 in any formalized form, including a verbal extension with named principal confirmation.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Trump and either Pezeshkian, Araghchi, or a confirmed Iranian MFA spokesperson publicly confirm the military ceasefire is extended for ≥30 days beyond June 15; OR if a signed MOU document (per F3 resolution) contains an explicit ceasefire extension clause covering through June 15. NO if the US or Iran resume active strikes against each other's forces or territory with neither party invoking self-defense/isolated-incident framing.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP minimum for ceasefire extension confirmation; US State Dept or Iran MFA official statement resolves independently. Trump Truth Social post alone is NOT sufficient without Iranian-side confirmation.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Isolated US airstrikes against IRGC-linked proxies in Iraq/Syria while US-Iran bilateral ceasefire holds = NOT collapse (consistent with current rules of engagement). Iranian proxy actions (Houthis, Iraqi militias) not directly ordered by Tehran = NOT collapse. 'Temporary pause' announced without a horizon date ≥ 30 days past June 15 = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: MOU or ceasefire extension document signed and confirmed by both Trump and Iranian principal
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; direct principal confirmation closes the biggest uncertainty gap.

indicators.name: US resumes active strikes against Iranian territory or IRGC inside Iran
indicators.expected_effect: -40pp toward YES if observed; would constitute ceasefire collapse.
